results.title: J&K Police announces Rs15 Lakh reward for LeT terrorist Mohammad Lateef Bhat wanted in murder of policeman
results.description: JAMMU: The police have announced a reward of Rs 15 lakh for any actionable information that leads them to the arrest of Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorist Mohammad Lateef Bhat, who was involved in the killing of a policeman on July 22 in Anantnag town. The security agencies have put up posters at prominent public places in Kashmir seeking actionable information leading to the arrest of LeT terrorist, announcing the reward. According to the police, Bhat was involved in the killing of Head Constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi on July 22 in Lal Chowk, a busy market area of Anantnag town. Qureshi was deployed in the area for ongoing Shri Amarnath yatra. The posters carry the photograph of the terrorist that was taken from CCTV grabs in the area when the terrorist was running away after killing the policeman. The posters say that the LeT terrorist hails from Kulgam district and is 22 years of age. Several phone numbers have been provided in the posters to contact the police. Read More: Assam Flood: RSS Swamsevaks reached 40,168 affected families with relief; Organised 50 medical camps Within days of Qureshi’s martyrdom, the administration of the Union Territory (UT) of Jammu and Kashmir gave an appointment in government job to his son. The announcement of the reward of Rs 15 lakh for catching the terrorist responsible for his death is continuing efforts of the police to finish terror ecosystem in J&K. Since the eruption of terrorist violence in 1989, so far over 1,600 police personnel have laid down their lives in the line of duty fighting terrorism. This toll includes regular officers, lower-ranked constables, and several hundred Special Police Officers (SPOs). Martyred policemen also include several Inspectors, Deputy SPs, Superintendents, and DIG-level officers. Around 515 SPOs have laid down their lives in the service of the nation while fighting terrorism, according to official records. Nine days after Qureshi’s killing, terrorists killed two non-local brick kiln labourers hailing from Chhatisgarh state in Kellam village of Kulgam district on July 31. A hunt is also on to trace the killers of these non-locals identified as Deepak and Bopinder. Deepak had died in the Government Medical College Hospital in Anantnag on the same day the terrorist shot him. Bhopinder was later shifted in a critical condition to the super speciality Sher-e-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences (SKIMS) in Srinagar. However, despite the best efforts of the doctors, Bopinder passed away in SKIMS Srinagar on August 1. The killings of non-locals were widely condemned by religious, political and social groups across the board. J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah had sanctioned ex gratia cash relief of Rs 10 lakh each for the next of kin of the two non-locals killed by the terrorists. Besides this amount released from the Chief Minister’s Relief Fund, the district administration of Kulgam had also released Rs 6 lakh for families of both the victims.

results.title: Reliance Retail acquires Furrl’s AI Styling Engine and commerce app
results.description: New Delhi: Reliance Retail Ventures (RRVL) acquired Furrl’s technology, including its AI Styling Engine and commerce app, as the retailer expanded the use of artificial intelligence across its consumer businesses. The Bengaluru-based company developed technology that uses consumer preferences and fashion catalogue data to recommend complete outfits rather than individual products. Following the acquisition, Furrl’s technology will support Reliance Retail’s personalisation and product discovery capabilities across its digital and omni-channel platforms. Founded by Esha Tiwary in 2022, Furrl initially focused on helping consumers discover products from direct-to-consumer fashion brands before developing its AI-based styling technology. The company said its platform covered more than 50,000 products from over 200 fashion and lifestyle brands. Its technology focused on catalogue intelligence, personalisation and outfit-level recommendations. Commenting on the development, Esha Tiwary, Founder of Furrl, said, "We built Furrl with one conviction: that fashion discovery is broken and AI can fundamentally change that. This acquisition enables our technology to reach millions of customers with Reliance Retail's scale, and is a powerful validation of what our team built."

results.title: Supreme Court questions HC order in Gadwal election case
results.description:
Telangana : The Supreme Court has questioned how an ex parte order could be passed when notices were not served on the person concerned, while hearing a challenge to the Telangana high court verdict that set aside the election of Gadwal MLA Bandla Krishna Mohan Reddy. The court indicated that it would ask the high [...]Telangana : The Supreme Court has questioned how an ex parte order could be passed when notices were not served on the person concerned, while hearing a challenge to the Telangana high court verdict that set aside the election of Gadwal MLA Bandla Krishna Mohan Reddy.

The court indicated that it would ask the high court to hear the election petition afresh.

SC questions service of notice before ex parte order

Krishna Mohan Reddy won the Gadwal assembly seat on a Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) ticket in 2018. D K Aruna subsequently filed an election petition in the high court, alleging discrepancies in the affidavit submitted by Reddy and seeking annulment of his election and a declaration that she be treated as the elected MLA.

After prolonged arguments, the high court in August 2023 declared Krishna Mohan Reddy's election invalid. It directed that Aruna, who had finished second in the election, be treated as the MLA with effect from December 12, 2018.

The high court also imposed a fine of ₹ 2,50,000 on Krishna Mohan Reddy for submitting an incorrect election affidavit.

Krishna Mohan Reddy challenged the high court judgment in the Supreme Court on August 31, 2023.

The petition came up for hearing on Thursday before a bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan.

Senior advocates Aditya Sondhi and Mohit Rao, appearing for Krishna Mohan Reddy, submitted that the notices issued by the high court had been served on a person identified as B Anantha Reddy and not on their client. Despite this, they said, the high court proceeded ex parte.

They also rejected the allegations that Krishna Mohan Reddy had concealed assets.

"The land concerned had been sold through a registered sale deed even before the election affidavit was filed. The bank accounts had only ₹ 16,000 to ₹ 18,000. While the high court issued notices to other respondents through newspaper publications, Krishna Mohan Reddy was treated differently," they argued.

Bench says HC could have issued fresh notice

Counsel for Aruna, Bina Madhavan, submitted that notices had been sent by registered post to the address mentioned in the affidavit. Under the General Clauses Act, a notice sent to the correct address should be deemed to have been served, she argued.

The bench, however, did not agree with the submission.

"When the signature on the acknowledgment is not that of Krishna Mohan Reddy, how can you conclude that the notice was served on him?" the bench asked.

The court observed that once the high court noticed the discrepancy in the signature on the acknowledgment, it could have issued a fresh notice or ordered publication of a notice in a newspaper.

Supreme Court indicates fresh hearing in election petition

In these circumstances, the bench indicated that it would set aside the ex parte order and direct the high court to hear the matter afresh.

Aruna's counsel sought time, following which the Supreme Court adjourned the matter to August 25. ]]>
